method: I chose to approach the assignment through writing rather than making an artwork.I first reviewed the theories and examples discussed in class, then compared them with my own experiences of watching films, TV series and ASMR videos.I focused on the difference between synchronisation and audiovisual congruence.
related_work: The McGurk Effect (McGurk and MacDonald, 1976) demonstrates how visual information can influence speech perception.Michel Chion's concepts of synchronisation, synchresis and added value helped me understand how sound and image can create a unified experience and influence meaning.I also considered Donnelly's discussion of sound-image synchronisation and Walter Murch's ideas about how sound can influence our interpretation of images.
conclusion_future_work: Through this week's learning and writing, I have developed a better understanding of how sound and image influence each other.I realised that sound does not always need to match an image perfectly to create a meaningful experience.I also began to question whether my expectations of a character's voice are influenced by my previous experiences and assumptions about appearance and personality.
results_discussion: I had some previous knowledge of post-production dubbing and had noticed how sound can communicate information and emotions through films and other visual works.However, I had never examined the relationship between sound and image in much detail.The McGurk Effect was particularly interesting because it demonstrated how visual information can influence what we think we hear, rather than simply helping us understand what we see.I also found the use of synchronised sound effects in *Tom and Jerry* interesting.The sounds often exaggerate the characters' movements, making actions feel more dramatic or humorous than they would without sound.This made me think about how sound can actively shape the way we interpret an image, rather than simply accompany it.Another concept I found interesting was *point of audition*.I had not previously paid much attention to whose listening perspective a film presents, even though this can influence how the audience experiences a scene.These examples helped me examine the relationship between sound and image more carefully, particularly how they influence perception and interpretation.For the assignment, I decided to explore synchronisation and audiovisual congruence through a short written reflection based on my viewing experiences.Rather than simply describing these concepts, I wanted to question why my expectations of sound and image seem to change depending on what I am watching.
title: week5
introduction: This week, we explored the relationship between sound and image, including the McGurk Effect, synchronisation, and how sound influences our perception of visual content.I was particularly interested in synchronisation and audiovisual congruence, so I chose to explore these concepts through writing, connecting them with my experiences of watching films, TV series and ASMR videos.
